findings.problem: Both decrement proofs need the same fact: the (i+1)-st dyadic Gram is the cutoff heat Gram at time `(R/2^i)^2/4`. Neither proof states this. Each one rebuilds an anonymous `hnext` from `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` and two positivity proofs, unfolds with `dyadicHeatGram_coe` inside `simp only`, and then runs `rw [hnext]`. The same block is pasted in two places in this file (lines 72–74 and 101–103) and a third time in SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean. A reader has to work out from the proof terms that this is the 'quarter of the squared radius' step.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a named lemma next to `dyadicHeatGram_coe`, before `variable {U}` on line 53:

```lean
/-- The next dyadic Gram is the cutoff Gram at a quarter of the current squared radius. -/
theorem dyadicHeatGram_succ_coe {R lambda : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (i : ℕ)
    (h : 0 < (R / (2 : ℝ) ^ i) ^ 2 / 4) :
    (dyadicHeatGram μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda (i + 1) : Euclidean n →L[ℝ] Euclidean n) =
      cutoffHeatGram μ hQ hk χ.weight.continuous (χ.hasCompactSupport μ hQ) U h p lambda :=
  (dyadicHeatGram_coe μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda (i + 1)).trans
    (cutoffHeatGram_time_congr μ hQ hk U χ _ h (dyadic_radius_square_succ R i))
```

Then replace each `have hnext := …` / `rw [hnext]` pair with a single rewrite placed before the `simp only`, e.g. in `dyadicHeatGram_upper`:

```lean
  rw [dyadicHeatGram_succ_coe μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda i
    (div_pos (sq_pos_of_pos hs) (by norm_num))]
  simp only [sub_apply, inner_sub_right, dyadicHeatGram_coe]
  simpa only [← hn] using hb
```

In `dyadicHeatGram_lower`, make the same change and keep the existing `simp only [dyadicBochnerMass_inner, …]`, `convert hb using 1` and `ring` steps.
findings.benefit: Each decrement proof loses a three-line block of positivity bookkeeping. What remains reads as: rewrite the next Gram as the quarter-time Gram, unfold, and apply the heat-increment bound. That is the mathematical idea. The dyadic halving step gets a name and a docstring and is proved once instead of being pasted three times. No automation is added: the new lemma is a plain `.trans` of two existing named lemmas.
